-sS: Stealth scan — checks each port without finishing the connection, so it's less likely to show up in the target's logs
-sT: Full connection scan — connects all the way to each port, so it's more likely to be logged than -sS
-sU: Also checks UDP ports, not just TCP — takes much longer
-sV: Tries to figure out what software/version is running on each open port
-sC: Runs a set of built-in checks (scripts) to learn more about each open service
-A: Turns on everything at once (guess the OS, check versions, run scripts, trace the route) — very thorough, but very easy for the target to notice
-O: Tries to guess the target's operating system
-Pn: Skips the initial "is this host online" check and scans it anyway — useful if the target blocks that check, but the scan may take longer
-n: Skips looking up domain names for IP addresses — makes the scan slightly faster
-F: Only checks the 100 most common ports instead of all of them — faster
--top-ports: Only checks the most common N ports — faster, but may miss less common services
-p-: Checks every port from 1 to 65535 — very thorough, but slow and easy to notice
--open: Only lists the ports that came back open
-f: Splits each check into smaller pieces — can slip past simple firewalls that only look at whole packets
--script: Runs the extra check named here — may send more traffic than a normal scan, depending on what that check does
-T0: Slowest possible speed setting — hardest for the target to notice
-T1: Very slow speed setting — hard for the target to notice
-T2: Slow, gentle speed setting — light load on the network and the target
-T4: Fast speed setting — good for your own lab network, but easier for the target to notice
-T5: Fastest possible speed setting — very easy to notice, and results may be less accurate
-v: Shows more detail on screen while the scan is running
--version-all: Tries harder to pin down the exact software version — more accurate but slower
